To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the Yang-Baxter equation for a bulk theory in the presence of a defect can only admit a simultaneous reflection-transmission solution if the transmission and reflection matrices commute with the defect degrees of freedoms.
in the presence of a defect the only theories that can have a simultaneous reflection and transmission are those with a rapidity independent defect scattering matrix.

(i) In the absence of a rapidity dependent impurity scattering matrix the only solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation with simultaneous transmission and reflection are the free Fermion and Boson, the Federbunch and their generalizations; (ii) In the presence of a rapidity independent impurity scattering matrix, the impurity can be described in terms of a rapidity-independent defect degrees of freedom.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of the scattering matrix for a quantum impurity coupled to a one dimensional quantum system with integrable bulk S-matrix, which is a solution of the Yang-Baxter equation.
a detailed analysis of the Yang-Baxter equation in the presence of a defect.
the question of the absence of simultaneous transmission and reflection in integrable impurities systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Yang-Baxer equations do not allow the possibility of a simultaneous reflection and transmission of particles at an impurity.
the Yang-Baxer equation in the presence of impurities can in general only have solutions which are simultaneous transmission and reflection, when the bulk and defect degrees of freedom decouple.
in integrable impurities systems, simultaneous transmission and reflection is only possible for the free Boson, Fermion and their anyonic generalizations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the only integrable impurities which admit excited states are the free Boson, Fermion, Federbush and their generalizations, and the only impurities which allow simultaneous transmission and reflection are the free Bosons and Fermions.
the Yang-Baxer equations for integrable impurity theories can only admit simultaneous transmission and reflection when the impurity is in the ground state.
the Yang-Baxer equation in general only permits solutions of simultaneous transmission and reflection when the defect degrees of freedoms are trivial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a defect in integrable systems can only allow for simultaneous transmission and reflection in the absence of anyons.
the Yang-Baxter equation in the presence of a defect is not a sufficient condition for the existence of simultaneous transmission and reflection.
the presence of an additional exchange of rapidities between the transmission and reflection coefficients is a generic feature of integrable systems in the presence of impurities.
